source.title: Finding Features in Neural Networks with the Empirical NTK

record.file_problem: The full LessWrong post is present. It summarizes a linked paper, but the paper itself and its figures are not included.
record.tranche_reason: It uses eNTK spectrum and feature-alignment measurements to track a modular-arithmetic grokking transition, a different measurement approach from the accuracy-based claim.
record.gate_note: The post reports a grokking transition for its modular-arithmetic model and describes eNTK spectrum and Fourier-feature alignment over training. The superposition-model results do not bear on these claim versions. The cited prior finding about eNTK tracking fine-tuning performance is not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: The post trains Gromov's modular-addition MLP, reports that it groks around epoch 90, and tracks eNTK spectrum and Fourier-feature alignment across the transition. This bears on V1 and, more directly, on V2's continuous-progress-measure claim. The evidence is weak: it is a by-product of a feature-discovery study, stated qualitatively, with one specified setting and no numbers in the text.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that the eNTK top eigenspaces align with ground-truth features in Toy Models of Superposition and in a modular-arithmetic MLP, and that eNTK spectrum evolution tracks the grokking transition. They frame this as preliminary evidence for a feature-discovery and phase-change-detection tool.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a modular-arithmetic MLP setting, but focuses on eNTK spectra and feature alignment rather than measuring the accuracy delay across training-set sizes.
record.method_sensitivity: The modular-arithmetic result is reported for p=29 and n=512; the post says other values were checked and were qualitatively similar, without specifying them.

fits_no_version.finding: The eNTK first cliff aligns with a/b Fourier families already at initialization, suggesting the kernel predicts Fourier-feature use before training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The structure of the generalizing algorithm for modular addition is partly predictable from the NTK at initialization.

record.peer_reviewed: LessWrong post; peer-review status not stated
record.problems: The post reports qualitative results without numerical accuracy or alignment values, gives no uncertainty estimates, and presents one specified modular-arithmetic setting for the grokking analysis. The actual linked paper is not included.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results were left out. Toy Models of Superposition findings do not bear on the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Training-set-size dependence of the delay; exact train/test accuracy trajectory (only in the omitted figure).
Removal of memorizing components; any quantitative lead of the progress measure over the accuracy jump.

missing.what: Train/test accuracy curves showing the grokking transition, including the training-accuracy saturation epoch
missing.locator: Figure: evolution of the full eNTK spectrum, left panel (figure not in text)

missing.what: Cosine-similarity values over epochs for the second-cliff alignment heatmaps
missing.locator: Heatmap figure for second cliff at different epochs (in linked paper arXiv:2510.00468)

record.verdict_notes: The post is a LessWrong summary of arXiv:2510.00468; the figures and the paper body are absent. Grokking is the setting here, not the target, and the results on V1 and V2 are qualitative. The authors say other p and n values were 'qualitatively similar' but do not report them. The Toy Models of Superposition results are unrelated to grokking.

versions.untested_parts: The post does not report the training and test accuracy values, their exact gap, or a training-set-size comparison showing that smaller training sets take longer.

It does not report removal of memorizing components. It reports eNTK spectrum changes and alignment with Fourier features, but does not establish that the complete generalizing circuit forms gradually or that the alignment quantitatively predicts the accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale or weight-norm sweep, or lazy-to-rich transition is tested.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning is tested.
No efficiency account, weight-decay intervention, critical dataset size, or ungrokking result is tested.
The post does not compare algorithms learned across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters.
No optimizer-instability or floating-point artifact control is tested.
